subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: What canonical inbound-media isolation boundary should OpenClaw use across agents and channels: account-scoped, agent/session-scoped, tenant-aware, explicit-share based, or a composed scope?
rationale: The source-backed privacy gap is real, but the durable storage/reference contract affects security boundaries, plugin behavior, sandbox staging, cleanup, and upgrades.

options.title: Define scoped contract first
options.body: Choose the ownership model, compatibility behavior, and explicit sharing semantics before implementation changes storage and staging paths.

options.title: Limit to account scoping
options.body: Implement the lower-friction account-based directory model, accepting that non-1:1 account-to-agent and tenant-sharing cases may need follow-up.

options.title: Defer broad core change
options.body: Keep only narrower channel-specific slices open until a maintainer sponsors a cross-channel core media-isolation design.

recommendation.title: Define scoped contract first
recommendation.body: Choose the ownership model, compatibility behavior, and explicit sharing semantics before implementation changes storage and staging paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The central media store, resolver, and channel media-save history most consistently route through this person, and they already reviewed this item as the broad tracker.
